#### Explaining Regular Expressions

Explain in simple words the languages described by following regular expressions. Avoid paraphrasing the regular expression!

1. `0(0|1)*0`

Binary strings of length at least two that start and end with `0`. The middle (which may be empty) can be any sequence of `0`s and `1`s. Equivalently: strings over `{0, 1}` that begin and end with `0`, including the two-character string `00`.

2. `([0]1)*[0]`

Strings over `{0, 1}` of odd length, made of alternating `0`s and `1`s, starting and ending with `0`. So the language is `{0, 010, 01010, 0101010, …}` — exactly the strings of the form $(01)^n 0$ for $n \ge 0$. Equivalently: an even number of `1`s, each `1` sandwiched between two `0`s, with one extra leading and one extra trailing `0` collapsing to a single `0` when the middle is empty.
